## Key Concepts for Editing a WordPress Homepage

This document summarizes the four primary methods for customizing your WordPress homepage, from basic settings to advanced tools.

### ## Getting Started: Static Page vs. Blog Feed

Before customizing, you must decide what your homepage will display.

- **Blog Feed**: The default setting. It shows your latest posts in chronological order. Customization is limited to cosmetic changes.
- **Static Page**: A custom-designed, fixed page. This is the preferred option for most business or portfolio sites as it offers full control over content and layout.

To change this setting, go to your WordPress Dashboard > **Settings** > **Reading** and under "Your homepage displays," select "**A static page**." Then, choose the page you want to use as your homepage.

---

### ## Method 1: The WordPress Customizer

The Customizer provides a theme-level interface for editing your site.

- **Access**: Navigate to **Appearance** > **Customize** from the dashboard or click "Customize" in the top admin bar when viewing your site.
- **Functionality**: Allows you to edit global elements that affect the entire site, including the homepage.
- **Customizable Elements**: 
    - **Header**: Site logo, navigation menus.
    - **Footer**: Widgets, copyright text.
    - **Global Settings**: Typography (fonts), color schemes, button styles, and page layout/container width.

> [!NOTE]
> The options available in the Customizer are **highly dependent on your active WordPress theme**. Themes like Astra offer advanced features like a drag-and-drop Header Builder, while others may have fewer options.

---

### ## Method 2: The Block Editor (Gutenberg)

The block editor is the default content editor in WordPress and can be used to build complex page layouts.

- **How it Works**: You build your page by adding and arranging different types of content "blocks" (e.g., paragraphs, headings, images, columns).
- **Editing**: Click on any block to edit its content and access specific settings (e.g., color, size, style) in the right-hand sidebar.
- **Extending Functionality**: You can install plugins that add new blocks and patterns to the editor. The video mentions **Spectra** as an example that enhances the block editor with more design elements.

---

### ## Method 3: Page Builders

Page builders are plugins that offer a visual, drag-and-drop interface for creating and editing pages.

- **Example**: The video demonstrates **SeedProd**.
- **Process**:
    1. **Create a New Page**: Start from a blank canvas or import a pre-designed template.
    2. **Drag & Drop**: Add elements (like images, buttons, text blocks) from a sidebar onto your page canvas.
    3. **Customize**: Click any element to edit its properties (content, style, etc.).
    4. **Publish**: Once finished, save the page and set it as your static homepage via **Settings > Reading**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Page Builder vs. Theme Builder**: A **page builder** typically edits the content area *between* the header and footer. A **theme builder** (often a pro feature of page builders like SeedProd) allows you to also design the header, footer, and other theme template parts.

---

### ## Method 4: The Full Site Editor (FSE)

This is the modern WordPress experience, available only with **block-based themes** (like the default Twenty Twenty-Three theme).

- **Access**: If using a block theme, the "Customize" option is replaced with "**Editor**" under the **Appearance** menu.
- **Core Feature: Styles**: FSE introduces a powerful **Styles** panel. You can browse and apply different global style variations with a single click, instantly changing your entire site's fonts, colors, and feel.
- **Granular Control**: You can also dive in and edit individual components like typography, colors, and layout without applying a full style preset.

> [!TIP]
> The Full Site Editor is a powerful but newer feature. If you want to use it, you must ensure you have a block-compatible theme installed and activated.
